A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MetaTT research work. The complete main texts and appendices are readable, and inspection of rendered pages supports matching their figures, tables, equations and relocated content.

before.justification: v2.pdf reports original MetaTT experiments on commonsense reasoning, GLUE and multi-task learning, together with DMRG, gradient and initialization analyses.

after.justification: v3.pdf retains original MetaTT evaluations and adds stability studies, AdaLoRA comparisons, and runtime and memory measurements in Appendices D–F.

M1.justification: The global 4D, 5D and task-dependent TT architectures, forward equations, implementation pseudocode and AdamW/SVD sweep procedure remain unchanged. The new Llama rank schedule configures an additional experiment; recommending MetaTT-4D does not introduce a different method.

E1.justification: Both versions cover the same GLUE tasks, three- and four-task joint learning, and eight commonsense evaluations. Commonsense15k is explicitly downsampled from the existing Commonsense170k data. The added analyses do not establish new task, domain or population coverage.

E2.justification: AdaLoRA, previously discussed without experimental comparison, becomes an evaluated comparator, including directly against MetaTT with and without DMRG in Figure 12. The principal comparator families in the existing commonsense, GLUE and multi-task comparisons remain unchanged; additional LoTR ranks are configurations of an existing baseline.

E3.justification: Appendices D–F introduce controlled learning-rate and rank sweeps, fixed-target-rank LoRA/AdaLoRA comparisons, and one-epoch Llama-2-7b experiments on 15k examples with a MetaTT rank schedule from 40 to 20. New runtime and memory protocols specify batch sampling, profiling intervals and rank controls. These substantially expand evaluation design within retained task coverage.

E4.justification: New analyses examine training stability, learning-rate and rank sensitivity, Gaussian/PiSSA/OLoRA initialization, DMRG versus fixed-rank Llama training, and computational overhead. Appendix I also reports contrasting effects of multi-step and single-step compression on full Commonsense170k. The earlier task-core gradient and MetaTT initialization analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Commonsense fine-tuning results change from explicitly single-run reporting in v2 to means and standard errors over three independent seeds in v3. Appendix D adds eight-seed stability evaluation with 95% confidence-interval half-widths, while Figure 12 reports errors over five runs. Existing GLUE and multi-task uncertainty reporting is largely retained.

E6.justification: Table 1 replaces single-run scores with multi-seed estimates: for example, Llama-2-7b MetaTT-4D rank 16 changes from 68.5 to 67.8(4) average accuracy. It also replaces the 7b rank-256 MetaTT entry with rank 64 and adds LoTR rank entries. New stability, adaptive-rank, runtime, memory and compression-failure findings substantially expand results. Existing GLUE per-task and multi-task scores are largely retained.

T1.justification: Appendix E.3 adds explicit computational-cost reasoning for per-layer full-matrix LoRA SVDs versus TT sweeps, including Equations 8–9 and model/rank cost ratios in Table 11. This formalizes an earlier qualitative argument. The original TT definitions, factorization equations and parameter-count analysis remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract and central global-adapter, multi-task and rank-adaptation contributions remain substantively unchanged. The conclusion now bounds demonstrated DMRG benefits to specified experimental regimes, identifies larger-dataset scaling as unresolved, and adds an explicit claim that the TT-SVD cost advantage becomes more favorable as models grow.

C2.justification: v3 explicitly states that multi-task inference requires task identity and acknowledges the RoBERTa-base accuracy gap: 70.5 average versus 74.9 for LoRA and 77.2 for MoE-LoRA. It recommends MetaTT-4D and reports that multi-step DMRG can reduce full Commonsense170k accuracy toward zero-shot levels, making compression schedules task- and scale-dependent. These materially sharpen applicability boundaries.

D1.justification: v3 adds LoRA/AdaLoRA hyperparameter tables, detailed DMRG schedules and implementation settings, profiling hardware and measurement procedures, and LoRETTA tensorization shapes. It also clarifies RoBERTa versus Llama initialization choices already partly documented in v2. The original MetaTT pseudocode and access information remain available.

R1.justification: v3 adds references to Compacter, shared hypernetworks, PiSSA, OLoRA and a statistical handbook. It acknowledges earlier multi-task parameter sharing through hypernetworks and develops the comparison with AdaLoRA. The main positioning relative to LoTR, FacT and LoRTA remains intact.

P1.justification: Most of the original narrative and method exposition is retained. Targeted rewrites clarify results and limitations, terminology is refined, and new appendices precede the retained experimental-details and implementation sections. Reproducibility and disclaimer headings become unnumbered; the additions do not constitute a wholesale narrative rewrite.

P2.justification: v3 adds numerous tables and multi-panel Figures 5–12 for stability, sensitivity and adaptive-rank comparisons. Table 2 gains averages and moves its MetaTT-5D rows into Table 22; the original initialization Figure 5 becomes Figure 13. The document template, typography, headings and placement of existing displays are also extensively reformatted.

improvement.justification: Three-seed commonsense results, a direct AdaLoRA comparison, and measured runtime and memory costs address important gaps in v2's empirical support. Explicit task-label requirements, multi-task accuracy tradeoffs and full-data DMRG failures improve transparency. New stability claims overgeneralize Table 7, which includes substantially larger uncertainty for some MetaTT settings, but the stronger validation and clearer applicability limits provide a substantial overall quality gain.
